source.title: Ground-truth evaluation of sparse autoencoder features on spatial, single-cell and language-model embeddings
source.authors: Amirhossein Shahsavand; Shayan Forghani; Saba Akbarzadeh; Fatemeh Mahdavi Sabet

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates SAE features against known concepts, including in a language-model residual stream, but does not test neuron poles or the explanation-fidelity claims in V1–V7.
record.gate_note: The language-model results below concern SAE features and rule-defined token classes, not individual neuron poles or explanations tested on new activating examples. They are recorded as findings about the claim's broader subject, with versions set to none. Biological and synthetic results do not bear on the language-model neuron claim.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates SAE features and rotation baselines (PCA, varimax, ICA) against known concepts, mostly in biological embeddings and once in Pythia-70m's residual stream. It never measures individual neurons or neuron poles, neuron explanations, attribution graphs or vision neurons. So it bears on none of V1–V7 and does not cite either original source. 'Discusses' is generous: it discusses feature interpretability in general, not this claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that reproducibility alone ranks features poorly. They recommend reporting SAE features with concept coverage and gene-program purity, against a rotation of the same embedding sparsified to the SAE's sparsity. The main evidence is biological; the language model is a secondary test case.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates BatchTopK SAE and rotation features against known concepts in embeddings; it does not audit neuron poles or test neuron explanations on held-out activating examples.
record.method_sensitivity: For Pythia-70m, consensus reproducibility was 0.62 with 50,000 tokens and 0.78 with one million tokens; the larger dictionary lowered reproducibility in Geneformer.

fits_no_version.finding: In Pythia-70m's layer-3 residual stream, the consensus SAE covered 8 of 8 token classes, against 6 for sparse varimax and 1 for varimax. Its reproducibility was 0.78, against 1.00 for both rotations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a small language model's residual stream, feature reproducibility and concept coverage diverge: rotations are more reproducible, while SAE features cover more rule-defined token classes.

fits_no_version.finding: Consensus SAE kNN balanced accuracy on token classes was 0.89, against 0.73 for sparse varimax and 0.91 for varimax.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE codes preserve token-class information about as well as a dense rotation and better than a sparsified one.

record.problems: The authors note that their ground truth is narrow, the language-model test uses Pythia-70m, and only two SAE variants were tested. The paper does not test neuron poles or explanation prediction on new activating examples.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were omitted. Biological and synthetic results were not extracted because they do not test language-model neuron claims.

untested.parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit shares; no neurons are examined.
Neuron-pole shares across dense and mixture-of-experts models and at scale; the only language model is Pythia-70m, with residual-stream SAE features.
InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons and recursive generalization.
Architecture and tool effects on neuron interpretability; the vision-model estimates.
Neuron-based attribution graphs without a replacement model.
Whether explanations from activating examples predict where a neuron fires.

record.verdict_notes: All rows compare the study's own consensus SAE with baselines on non-neuron directions, so none can link to a version. No neuron-level or explanation-scoring results exist in the text, so nothing is missing. Biological and synthetic results were correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Neuron-pole job counts and the Qwen3-32B audit.
Neuron-pole shares across dense and mixture-of-experts models and at large scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron and recursive generalization.
Vision-model neuron interpretability, architecture and tool effects, and the stated InceptionV1-sized estimates.
Attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons.
Whether explanations fitted to activating examples predict where a neuron fires.
Automated simulation-based scores of neuron explanations on new text.

tranche.reason: Evaluates SAE and rotation features against known concepts in embeddings (mostly biological; Pythia-70m layer-3 residual stream once). Never measures neurons, neuron poles, neuron explanations or attribution graphs; neither tests nor uses any version.

source_check.notes: Pythia-70m (layer-3 residual stream, 8 rule-defined token classes) is a secondary test beside biological embeddings; all rows are SAE-vs-rotation method comparisons, not neuron measurements, so they bear on no version. Table S5 gives LM consensus R1 0.78 ± 0.00 (symmetric); kNN uses 20,000 held-out tokens.
